slippy-map zoom levels 0-22 and the 256/512 tile pixel size are protocol constants of the XYZ tile scheme, not visual values
geospatial thresholds in packages/core (alert radii in metres, haversine constants, bearing degrees) are physical-world distances, not screen lengths; they must never be remapped by a display mode

the round watch face canvas is a fixed 384x384 device surface read directly from the design source (width:384px appears 31 times in 'Flockys Watch.dc.html'); it is a viewBox dimension, not a spacing value

the <meta name="theme-color"> value is mirrored by hand from --fwm-bg in apps/pwa/src/styles/tokens.css because the browser reads it before any stylesheet loads and cannot resolve var(); keep the two in sync whenever --fwm-bg changes

the manifest is a build artifact generated by scripts/generate-assets.mjs, which reads background_color and theme_color from apps/pwa/src/styles/tokens.json; the literal here is the token value emitted, not a value authored by hand, so editing this file to fix a colour would be the actual mistake

these are the media-query breakpoints in the surface-detection snippet reproduced verbatim from section 06 of 'Flockys Design System.dc.html', which the design contract requires be used exactly as written; they select which layout runs (phone / watch-round / watch-square / dash) and are never painted, so a --fwm-* token would be the wrong abstraction and would let a theme mode change which surface a device resolves to

the CCTV mark SWEEP draws for a camera, supplied as artwork rather than derived from the brand eye. It is a MASK, not a picture: white-on-transparent, so an SVG over a filled rect renders it in the state hue and along the blend ramp. That is why it is not an and why it can carry state at all -- a raster cannot take a fill, which ruled out both the colour emoji and an exploratory traced path that reached only IoU 0.45 against the source. Regenerate with scripts/generate-camera-mask.mjs.

the dynamic viewport height is a layout PRIMITIVE, not a design value: it is what the app shell is bounded to so a screen can scroll internally under a pinned header and dock. There is no --fwm-* token for 'the viewport' and inventing one would be a token meaning 'ask the browser'. 100dvh over 100vh on purpose -- dvh tracks a mobile browser's collapsing address bar and vh does not, which is what makes a bottom bar jump on scroll. `height: 100%` is declared immediately before it as the fallback.

an SVG font-size inside the dial's viewBox is a coordinate in the scope's own 343-unit space, not a CSS length on the page: the dial is scaled from 343 units to roughly 520px, so a type token at 10 renders near 15px on screen -- bigger than the header. No --fwm-text-* token can express a size in another coordinate system, and inventing one would be a token that means a different number everywhere it is used. Same class of value as the marker radii, which are attributes for the same reason.

an SVG font-size and letter-spacing inside the dial's viewBox are coordinates in the scope's own 343-unit space, not CSS lengths on the page: the dial is scaled from 343 units to roughly 520px, so a --fwm-text-* token renders far larger here than it does in the header. Same class of value as the marker radii and the cluster counts, which are attributes for the same reason. No token can express a size in another coordinate system.

a RATIO to the title's type size, not a length. The brand mark must be larger than the title beside it on every screen and in every theme mode, and the titles are different sizes -- a fixed --fwm-icon-size was barely bigger than a 19px title and would be SMALLER than a larger one. `em` resolves against the inherited font size, which is exactly the relationship being expressed; no --fwm-* token can state 'half again as big as whatever this is next to'. Raised from 1.5em through 1.62em to 2em: at 1.5 the eye sat almost exactly on the title's cap height and read as part of the word rather than as the thing the word is beside.

not a colour: pass one of the coverage field accumulates DENSITY in the alpha channel with `lighter` compositing, and pass two replaces every RGB triple with the token-derived ramp before anything is shown. White is the only value that accumulates without tinting the result -- any --fwm-* token here would bias the density it is measuring, and the visible palette does come from tokens (see HEAT_STOP_TOKENS)

the single neutral used for EVERY token when there is no document to read them from, which is only ever a headless environment. It is deliberately not a palette: a per-token fallback table would be a second copy of the design system -- the exact thing this file exists to prevent -- and it would be the copy nobody updates. A map rendered entirely in grey is obviously wrong, which is how a missing document should fail

upstream Protomaps basemap sprites and Noto Sans glyph ranges, vendored verbatim by scripts/vendor-basemap-assets.mjs and pinned to a commit; they are third-party map iconography and font atlases, not brand imagery, and altering them to satisfy the brand-derivation rule would corrupt the sprite sheet the style indexes by pixel offset

a MEDIA QUERY breakpoint, and CSS media queries cannot read custom properties -- `@media (max-width: var(--x))` is invalid by spec, so a token is not available here however much one is wanted. The value is measured rather than chosen: the RADAR header's count group needs 219px of content against 209px available at 390px, so 26.5rem is where the wordmark has to give way to the reading. See the note above the rule.

a canvas fillStyle must be a colour STRING - there is no var() in a 2D context - and this one is assembled from --fwm-sweep-hue read off the element at start, so the design value still lives in tokens.css and follows every theme. Only the hsl() syntax is in code, and only for the per-particle alpha and hue jitter a token cannot express.
